skill.name: azure-quotas
skill.description: Check Azure quota limits, usage, and available regional capacity with Azure CLI workflows and helper scripts.
skill.summary: Plan Azure deployments by comparing quota limits, current usage, and available capacity across regions.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: Most markdown detections are false positives caused by backticked Azure CLI examples, fenced code blocks, and Microsoft documentation links. Confirmed risks are limited to helper scripts that run Azure CLI read operations against the current subscription. No evidence found for audit bypass language, credential exfiltration, or hidden network endpoints.

remediation.issue: Helper scripts install the Azure quota CLI extension automatically.
remediation.suggestion: Split extension installation into a separate setup step or require explicit confirmation before installing it.

remediation.issue: Scripts use the active Azure subscription when no subscription ID is supplied.
remediation.suggestion: Require SubscriptionId or display the selected subscription and ask for confirmation before continuing.

remediation.issue: The quota increase workflow can submit changes to Azure subscription quota settings.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear confirmation step and explain approval impact before any quota update command is run.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Azure CLI Extension Installation
semantic_findings.description: Both helper scripts install the Azure quota CLI extension when it is missing. Automatic dependency installation changes the user CLI environment and can fetch executable code.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The scripts explicitly run az extension add --name quota when the extension is absent. This is a clear setup side effect, even though it supports the skill purpose.

semantic_findings.title: Quota Increase Workflow Requires Explicit Consent
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents an Azure CLI quota update workflow that submits a quota increase request for a subscription. This is a legitimate feature but changes Azure account state.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow is clearly labeled as requesting a quota increase and includes an az quota update example. The side effect is explicit and should require user approval.

content.value_statement: Azure deployments fail when quota limits are unknown or region capacity is insufficient. This skill guides quota discovery, usage checks, region comparison, and quota increase requests with Azure CLI.
actual_capabilities: Lists Azure quota limits and current usage for supported resource providers.
Calculates available capacity for one quota or all quotas in a region.
Compares quota availability across candidate Azure regions.
Maps ARM resource types to quota resource names through discovery steps.
Explains quota increase requests and request status checks.
Provides Bash and PowerShell helper scripts for quota checks.
limitations: Requires Azure CLI authentication and the quota extension.
Only covers providers supported by the Azure quota API.
Quota increase approval depends on Azure policies and service availability.
Examples require valid subscription, provider, region, and resource names.

use_cases.title: Validate deployment capacity
use_cases.description: Check quota limits and current usage before deploying virtual machines, networking resources, or platform services.

use_cases.title: Select an Azure region
use_cases.description: Compare available quota across regions to choose a location with enough capacity for planned workloads.

use_cases.title: Resolve quota exceeded errors
use_cases.description: Identify the relevant quota name, review current usage, and prepare a quota increase request when needed.

prompt_templates.title: Check a provider quota
prompt_templates.prompt: Check Azure quota usage for Microsoft.Compute in eastus. Explain the command and summarize available capacity.

prompt_templates.title: Compare candidate regions
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare vCPU quota for standardDSv3Family across eastus, eastus2, and westus2 for my subscription.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate quota errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me resolve a QuotaExceeded error for Azure Container Apps in centralus. Identify the quota name and next action.

prompt_templates.title: Plan capacity and fallback
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a capacity plan for a 200 vCPU deployment across three regions. Include quota checks, increase request steps, and fallback options.

output_examples.input: Check Microsoft.Compute quotas in eastus before a VM deployment.
output_examples.output: A concise quota summary with limit, current usage, available capacity, and any resource families that need attention.
A ranked region comparison showing which locations have enough available quota and which require an increase request.
A troubleshooting path that identifies the likely quota, verifies current usage, and recommends an increase request or alternate region.

best_practices: Run read-only quota checks before deployment planning.
Confirm subscription and region before executing any Azure CLI command.
Request a buffer above immediate capacity needs when Azure allows it.
anti_patterns: Assuming ARM resource type names match quota resource names.
Treating a missing limit or No Limit response as unlimited capacity.
Submitting quota increase requests without confirming business need and region.

faq.question: Does this skill require Azure credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. Azure CLI must be installed and authenticated before quota checks can access subscription data.

faq.question: Can it request quota increases?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Azure CLI quota increase workflows, but users should review every change before execution.

faq.question: Does it support every Azure provider?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on providers supported by the Azure quota API and points to service limits docs for gaps.

faq.question: Why compare regions?
faq.answer: Quota availability varies by region, so comparison helps avoid failed deployments and capacity delays.

faq.question: Can I use it in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it change Azure resources automatically?
faq.answer: Read-only checks query quotas. Helper scripts may install the quota extension, and increase commands require explicit execution.
